bindings.finding: Corresponding loci and AA/Aa/aa distinguish allele combination from phenotype under the stated fictional autosomal model.
The same complete-dominance map shows AA/Aa sharing a scored phenotype while aa differs; dominance does not imply frequency, value or universal mechanism.

Follow the heterozygous locus in the Aa panel. For this comparison, assign A to the long teal homologue and a to the long orange homologue of the2n=4 count model; the short chromosome type does not carry the tracked locus. Homologue separation and later sister separation put one tracked allele in each final product, two A and two a in this no-crossing-over model. The Punnett square then combines independently contributed gametes from two Aa parents. This explains one-locus segregation without claiming independence of every pair of loci.

Parents, tester gamete and expression assumptions precede the1:1 Aa/aa prediction. This supports the restored source-slide26 model/notation requirement without the source simplistic human-trait examples.
AA and Aa alternatives have different predictions with aa. An aa offspring identifies the unknown as Aa under assumptions; four dominant offspring remain possible from Aa with probability1/16.

Each cell combines one gamete from each parent, at weight1/4. Aa and aA are one unphased genotype reached by different parental paths. Complete dominance yields3/4 versus1/4 phenotypes; it is not a four-offspring schedule.

Unequal genotype weights are retained when excluding aa in a fully penetrant recessive model, yielding2/3 carrier probability conditional on unaffected. Product-rule independence and exclusive parent-identified paths are distinguished. v2 explicitly uses parent subscripts so Aa/aA are not mistakenly treated as different unphased genotypes.

All16 genotypes and1/16 weights are explicit for AaBb×AaBb. Category counts9/3/3/1 match complete dominance and independence. The model is distinct from the two-locus recessive-tester cross and is not universal under linkage.

priorReview.finding: The 2n=4 starting cell has four duplicated chromosomes. Each product after meiosis I has two duplicated chromosomes and one homologous set. Counts refer to the outlined products, not an undivided anaphase cell. Long/short marks denote types and colours distinguish homologues; crossing over is explicitly omitted. The same count model continues meiosis I products through sister separation to four haploid products with two unduplicated chromosomes each. There is no intervening S phase. Crossing over is omitted in this model, so its matching final symbols must not imply that actual meiosis II products are always genetically identical or four equally functional gametes.
